en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: Traditional. 'шкрипците' I read as parts of the loom, and 'мори џанам' as an endearing refrain.

lines.en: The bride was weaving cloth, hey my dear,
the loom pedals sang her a song.
From below comes a stranger, hey my dear,
a stranger, a young foreigner.

lines.cyr: Фатило коњче за узда, мори џанам,
lines.lat: Fatilo konjče za uzda, mori džanam,
lines.en: He took his horse by the bridle, hey my dear,
and headed straight for home.

lines.cyr: Право си трга за дома, мори џанам,
lines.lat: Pravo si trga za doma, mori džanam,
lines.en: He headed straight for home, hey my dear,
to that young bride.
The bride says, she speaks, hey my dear:
- Stranger, young foreigner,

lines.cyr: не врти коњче кај мене, море лудо,
lines.lat: ne vrti konjče kaj mene, more ludo,
lines.en: do not turn your horse by me, you foolish one,
my young man is in a foreign land.
- Bride, comely and beautiful, hey my dear,
I will ask you, I will question you:

lines.cyr: дали си млада невеста, мори џанам,
lines.lat: dali si mlada nevesta, mori džanam,
lines.en: are you a young bride, hey my dear,
or are you a black-clad widow?
- Stranger, young foreigner, hey my dear,
I am not a black-clad widow,

lines.cyr: туку сум млада невеста, море лудо,
lines.lat: tuku sum mlada nevesta, more ludo,
lines.en: but I am a young bride, you foolish one,
my sweetheart is in a foreign land.
- Bride, comely and beautiful, hey my dear,
well, since you are a young bride,

lines.cyr: фати си коњче за узда, мори џанам,
lines.lat: fati si konjče za uzda, mori džanam,
lines.en: take your horse by the bridle, hey my dear,
I am your sweetheart.
